Strongest optimist result: a residents' pact backed by a grim boycott (after any sale all three refuse everything; fleet gets 0) is a subgame-perfect equilibrium of the repeated game iff delta >= 2/3, because at k=2 no single resident can alter the outcome, so "all refuse" is a stage Nash equilibrium every period; the fleet's best break (all four slots, bribe residents 1 and 2 at h_i + 1.5/(1-delta), total 5 + 3/(1-delta), nets 13.5 - 3/(1-delta) once) beats staying at 1.5/(1-delta) only when delta < 2/3. Holds at 0.8 and 0.95, fails at 0.5. Finite boycotts of T=4 (delta 0.8) or T=3 (0.95) periods suffice on paper. What this rests on, computed: in the boycott phase a resident has nothing left to lose, so accepting any bribe above her harm is weakly dominant; if the fleet can post a public conditional offer ("I pay both of you if both consent"), it buys through the boycott at bribes of 5 for 13.5 a period, and anticipating that, its pact-phase deviation pays 21.0 / 52.5 / 210.0 against staying at 3.0 / 7.5 / 30.0 at delta 0.5 / 0.8 / 0.95: the pact breaks at every delta. The program-equilibrium rescue (each resident's agent consents only to pact terms and only while the other two run the same program) is a Nash equilibrium whose breaking needs the fleet plus two residents to switch programs together (bribes 3.5 + 4.5 = 8, fleet nets 10.5 against 1.5): Nash, not coalition-proof (Bernheim, Peleg and Whinston 1987 [likely]), exactly the river's row-10 finding with the breaking coalition now three parties, the same size as the pact. So on the instance the pact at k=2 is a coordination race between two three-party coalitions, residents' and fleet's, and the only compute dial that decides a coordination race is speed, which the single principal holds.

ENFORCER. The instance's price for a platform enforcer is its clause language, and that price is a pie cost I can enumerate [sure]: four slots: 6 parametric / 5 arbitrary; two clauses with day={M,D}, night={E,N}: 5.5 / 5 (the arbitrary optimum MD is in this menu); two clauses with day={M,D,E}, night={N}: 6 / 4.5; all-or-nothing: 5.5 / 4. In Nash-product terms under the equal split: 5.06, 3.57, 5.06, 3.57 parametric; 2.44, 2.44, 1.60, 1.00 arbitrary. Optimist reading: a four-clause standard form costs nothing; the worst form costs 30% of the product parametric and 59% arbitrary; and the two-clause forms show the cost is a property of which partition the enforcer writes, not of enforcement. What it concedes: whoever writes the standard form picks the pie, which makes the platform an incumbent of its own kind. At k=3 the enforcer is not needed for the residents' pact at all (above); it is needed at k=2, where its job is precisely to make "refuse the bribe" a commitment rather than a weakly dominated tie.

BUDGETS (finite budgets on, k=3). The river's row 1 (extraction: product 0.07 to a peak 1.11 to 0.0002) is a property of the take-it-or-leave-it protocol, not of estimation. Under a fair-split CONVENTION (the proposer picks the schedule maximising its estimated surplus and offers every party a quarter of its estimated pie; responders accept iff their own true gain is nonnegative; the fleet knows p and estimates s_i, the residents know their s_i and estimate p_t), estimation compute is a public good [sure, simulated]: fleet proposes, e_f = 1 / 0.3 / 0.1 / 0.03: deal rate 45.5% / 93.4% / 100% / 100%, E[pie] 2.38 / 5.51 / 5.99 / 6.00, gains (0.51; 0.49, 0.71, 0.67) / (1.40; 1.36, 1.39, 1.37) / (1.50; 1.50, 1.50, 1.50) / 1.5 each, product 0.12 / 3.61 / 5.04 / 5.06, residents' share 0.79 / 0.75 / 0.75 / 0.75, floor 0.49 / 1.36 / 1.50 / 1.50, nobody ever below 0, expectations already count failed deals as zero. Residents propose, e_N = 1 / 0.3 / 0.1: deal 76% / 99.9% / 100%, product 1.31 / 4.97 / 5.06, floor 1.04 / 1.47 / 1.50. Random proposer at the instance's budget ratios, level e = 1 / 0.3 / 0.1: 1:1 product 0.49 / 4.25 / 5.05; 10:1 product 2.17 / 5.01 / 5.06 with gains (1.21; 1.21, 1.22, 1.22) at level 1; 1:10 product 1.17 / 4.28 / 5.05. Asymmetry HELPS everyone relative to equal low budgets and the better-funded side takes no larger share: residents' share 0.75 to 0.77 throughout. Exploitability, bounded: if the proposer shades its declared harms by Delta and the responders audit the implied pie against their own estimate to one standard error, the fleet's excess take is Delta/4 with Delta <= 4*sqrt(3)*e_N: at e_N = 1 / 0.3 / 0.1 the fleet takes 3.23 / 2.02 / 1.67 against 0.92 / 1.33 / 1.44 each for residents, product 2.54 / 4.72 / 5.02; the mirror (residents shading, fleet auditing with error e_f*sqrt(11.25)) gives fleet 0.66 / 1.25 / 1.42 at e_f = 1 / 0.3 / 0.1, product 3.73 / 4.96 / 5.05. So the tilt is bounded by the WEAKER side's own budget, not the ratio: "give everyone a moderately capable agent" (e = 0.1) caps the stronger side's excess at 0.17 of 6. [sure as arithmetic; the audit rule is my own stylisation, not the instance's text.] Arbitrary switch on, finite budgets [sure, simulated]: the fleet's scalar estimator cannot see resident 3's interaction term, so when the fleet proposes it picks MDE (never MD), pays resident 3 her additive harm plus a quarter, and her true gain is 0 plus noise: e_f = 1 / 0.3 / 0.1 / 0.01: deal 32% / 48% / 50% / 50%, resident 3's gain 0.36 / 0.19 / 0.065 / 0.007, product 0.013 / 0.054 / 0.025 / 0.003, peaking at a middling budget then falling to zero as the estimator converges on the wrong model. When the residents propose (they hold the term): e_N = 1 / 0.3 / 0.1: picks MD 38% / 82% / 100%, product 0.33 / 2.23 / 2.44 (the maximum 2.44). Random proposer at 1:1 tops out at 0.63 with resident 3 at 0.66. So under arbitrary preferences the right fix is not symmetric speed but letting the informed side propose or report.

INCUMBENT. Wealth effects on, k=3, limit [sure, optimised]: the Nash-product maximiser in utility units gives money gains (1.634; 1.535, 1.535, 1.296): the poorest and most-harmed resident takes the least money and the fleet the most, residents' share 0.728, but resident 3's utility gain is 0.500 against 0.143 for residents 1 and 2 and 0.016 for the fleet; the equal-money split loses only 1.4% of the product (1.628e-4 against 1.651e-4); the floor in utility units is the fleet's. No incumbent tilt worth the name arises from wealth. Speed: the row-6 number transfers (above), and on the instance the single principal's speed is also what decides the k=2 coalition race. Entitlement: at k=2 the excluded party is resident 3 in every fleet-plus-two coalition, because her consent is the dearest (harm 8 of the 13 under all four slots): the most-harmed resident is structurally the one left out, floor -8, at any budget.

KRIER'S REPLY, stated against my finding: his bargaining club is the residents' coordination at k=2; his option fee and court are the commitment that turns "refuse the bribe" from a weakly dominated tie into a binding promise; his standard forms are the clause language. On the instance the reply holds: with those supplied, k=2 restores k=3 and 1.5 each, and the four-clause form costs nothing. What it concedes: (1) each is a state-backed or platform institution, not a consequence of giving everyone an agent; (2) the club is only wanted at k<3, since at k=3 a club with a fixed internal split lowers the product from 5.06 to 3.0; (3) forming the club is a race against the fleet's public conditional offer, a coalition of three against a coalition of three, which speed decides; (4) the writer of the standard form picks up to 30% (parametric) or 59% (arbitrary) of the Nash product; (5) under arbitrary preferences his devices do nothing until the informed side is the one proposing or reporting.

rows_attacked.what_it_would_become: Split by consent rule. At k=3 (any switches): retire; the pact is unnecessary, the equal split is self-enforcing at every delta without an enforcer, and a bloc with a fixed internal split lowers the product 5.06 to 3.0. At k=2 (no enforcer, recurring): the pact is a subgame-perfect equilibrium iff delta >= 2/3 under a residents' boycott, but the boycott rests on refusing a weakly dominant bribe, so a fleet that can post a public conditional offer breaks it at every delta (deviation 21.0/52.5/210.0 against 3.0/7.5/30.0); the program-equilibrium pact is Nash, not coalition-proof, and the breaking coalition is three parties like the pact. Row reads: "the pact at k<3 is a coordination race between two three-party coalitions that speed decides". Status: computed (pact_k2.py, followups.py).

The enforcer's cost is a clause-language cost, enumerated: pie 6/5.5/6/5.5 parametric and 5/5/4.5/4 arbitrary under four slots / two (MD|EN) / two (MDE|N) / all-or-nothing; Nash product 5.06/3.57/5.06/3.57 and 2.44/2.44/1.60/1.00. Row reads: "a four-clause standard form costs nothing; whoever writes the form picks up to 30% (parametric) or 59% (arbitrary) of the product; the enforcer is unneeded at k=3 and at k=2 is the commitment that makes refusing a bribe binding". Status: computed (instance.py).

Parametric arm: under a fair-split convention with responders accepting iff own gain >= 0, estimation compute is a public good: product 0.12/3.61/5.04 (fleet proposes, e_f 1/0.3/0.1), 1.31/4.97/5.06 (residents propose), and at the instance's ratios 10:1 beats 1:1 for every party (2.17 vs 0.49 at level 1) with the residents' share fixed at 0.75-0.77; shading is bounded by the weaker side's own audit error (fleet's excess take 0.17 at e_N=0.1). Arbitrary arm: a scalar estimator in the uninformed side's hands drives the product to zero as its budget grows (0.013/0.054/0.025/0.003 at e_f 1/0.3/0.1/0.01, resident 3 to 0.007), while the informed side proposing reaches the maximum 2.44. Row reads: "estimation's sign is set by the protocol (extraction vs convention), not by the budget; the tilt from asymmetry is bounded by the weaker side's level; and compute cannot buy a non-scalar from the wrong side". Status: computed (budgets.py, followups.py); the convention and audit rule are the reviewer's stylisation.

Wealth effects produce no tilt worth the name: the utility-unit maximiser gives money (1.634; 1.535, 1.535, 1.296), residents' share 0.728, and the equal-money split loses 1.4% of the product; resident 3's utility gain (0.50) is the largest and the fleet's (0.016) the smallest. The incumbent channels that survive on the instance are speed (row-6 number transfers at the same pie and party count) and exclusion at k=2, where the most-harmed resident is left out of every fleet-plus-two coalition because her consent is dearest (floor -8 at any budget). Row reads: "the incumbent is whoever assembles a coalition of three first; wealth is not a channel under the criterion". Status: computed (wealth.py, instance.py); speed number from the state [likely].

optimists.answer: On the instance, more computation for bargaining agents produces better outcomes under the Nash product for every party, with no tilt toward the better-funded side, under three conditions that hold together: every party holds a veto (k=3), the protocol is a fair-split convention rather than take-it-or-leave-it, and the information to be estimated is a scalar; then estimation compute is a public good (product 0.12 to 5.06 as error falls 1 to 0.03, residents' share fixed at 3/4, nobody below no deal, and 10:1 budgets better for everyone than 1:1 at the same level), shading is capped by the weaker side's own budget (0.17 of 6 at e=0.1), the pact needs no enforcer, and wealth effects move the poorest resident's money by 0.2 while her utility gain is the largest. Each condition fails on a switch the instance has: at k=2 the pact is a coordination race between a residents' coalition of three and a fleet coalition of three that speed decides, with the most-harmed resident the one excluded (floor -8 at any budget); under arbitrary preferences the uninformed side's scalar compute converges on the wrong deal (product to 0.003 as its error vanishes) until the informed side proposes; and a platform enforcer's standard form costs 0 to 59% of the product depending on who writes it. Krier's secondary institutions supply the three conditions and his reply holds on the instance, but what it concedes is the essay: they are institutions, the club hurts at k=3 (5.06 to 3.0) and is wanted only at k<3, forming it is a race the single principal's speed wins, and the form-writer is a new incumbent. For whom: under the three conditions, everyone equally; under any switch, whoever moves first, holds the dearest consent, writes the form, or holds the non-scalar information.

Rows retired: none outright; pact at k=3 recommended for retirement. Finite-budget column: the parametric numbers above at e = 1 / 0.3 / 0.1 beside the limit 5.06; the arbitrary numbers beside the limit 2.44. River-dependence: none of the above uses the river's numbers; the row-6 speed number transfers by identical pie and party count [likely]. Mission touched: no; one note for Dan, not a change: in utility units the floor check names the fleet (gain 0.016) as the worst-off party, because its endowment is 100, which the mission may not intend.

missing_cases.case: A. The chain store: the fleet is the party in many bargains. One fleet agent negotiates the same schedule with M successive neighbourhoods, each a fresh triple of one-shot residents who can see how the fleet treated earlier neighbourhoods; the fleet has a prior probability mu of being a type that never pays above measured harm.
missing_cases.why_the_instance_cannot_express_it: The instance is one neighbourhood with the same three residents. Its recurring switch repeats the bargain with the same counterparties, so both sides are long-run players and the folk theorem's symmetric set applies; it has no arm in which one side persists while the other is replaced, so reputation cannot be built by one side and not the other, and nothing in it carries the fleet's record from one bargain to the next.
missing_cases.smallest_change_that_would: Add to the recurring switch a 'fresh residents each period' arm: the resident triple is redrawn each period (same exposures and sensitivities), the fleet persists, past outcomes are public, and the fleet's type is tough with probability mu in {0.05, 0.2}. The schedule, harms and pie (6 at MDE, all switches otherwise off) are unchanged.
missing_cases.why_it_matters_for_the_question: A long-run player facing a sequence of short-run opponents approaches its commitment (Stackelberg) payoff as the horizon grows (Fudenberg and Levine 1989 [likely, not read this session]; Kreps and Wilson 1982 [likely]). On the instance that is the fleet taking the whole pie: (6; 0, 0, 0) per neighbourhood, Nash product 0, floor 0, residents' share 0, efficient schedule still run. It is the open-system reading of 'already one principal rather than many' and it makes the state's symmetric rows (equal sampling, nobody systematically first) unavailable by construction: the party in many bargains is the one with the history. More compute (speed, commitment reliability) for the fleet raises how fast it approaches the limit; more compute for one-shot residents buys nothing they can carry forward.

missing_cases.case: B. Competing neighbourhoods: unanimity inside, divide and conquer across. The fleet needs the consent of one of two identical resident triples (A or B); the traffic, and the harm, go wherever it signs.
missing_cases.why_the_instance_cannot_express_it: The instance has one neighbourhood and its consent rule k acts only within it; the fleet's only alternative to a deal is the reroute at 3 per slot, a pure cost paid to nobody. It cannot represent the fleet choosing between counterparties, which is the open system's version of substitutes between consents.
missing_cases.smallest_change_that_would: Duplicate the resident triple once (same e_i, s_i) and let the fleet contract with whichever triple it chooses; k = 3 inside each triple; the losing triple bears no harm. Everything else at baseline.
missing_cases.why_it_matters_for_the_question: The two triples are perfect substitutes, so they undercut each other to their joint harm: transfers (1, 2.5, 4) = 7.5 for MDE, residents' gains 0 over no deal, fleet 6, Nash product 0, floor 0 [sure, Bertrand on the enumerated harms]. Unlike the river's k = 1, nobody ends below no deal, because the loser is not harmed; but the residents' share goes to zero at any compute budget, with the veto intact in every neighbourhood. The consent rule the essay treats as a protection protects nothing once the fleet can shop across bargains, and the open system always offers a second neighbourhood.

missing_cases.case: C. Linked bargains: residents are also the fleet's customers, and the fleet can bundle the two deals. Each resident gets a value v_i from being served (v = (1, 1, 3), resident 3 depends most on deliveries) that the fleet can withhold.
missing_cases.why_the_instance_cannot_express_it: Every resident's only stake in the fleet is harm; no resident has anything the fleet can withhold, so the no-deal point is fixed at (0; 0, 0, 0) by the rule and cannot be moved by a party. Bundling, the state's open row on Snow's bike lane, needs a second good on the same table.
missing_cases.smallest_change_that_would: Give each resident a service value v_i, realised only if a schedule deal is signed, with v = (1, 1, 3) and zero cost to the fleet. Baseline switches otherwise.
missing_cases.why_it_matters_for_the_question: The bundled pie is 6 + 5 = 11 and the symmetric Nash split gives each party 2.75 over the bundled no-deal; in money over the clean-and-served river that is +1.75, +1.75, -0.25 for the residents and +2.75 for the fleet, residents' money share of the 6 falls from 0.75 to 0.54, and resident 3, the most harmed and the poorest, is paid less than his harm [sure, computed]. The Nash product on the bundled origin rises to 57 from 5.06, so the criterion reports the bundled deal as much better while the worst-off resident is worse off than before the bundle existed. The no-deal origin that the mission's criterion measures from is, in an open system, a choice of the party with more than one thing to trade, and compute spent on finding bundles moves it.

missing_cases.case: D. Cross-bargain scoring of the weak side: a resident whose agent refuses is marked as a holdout in a reputation system that the airport, the landlord and the next fleet also read, costing r in those other bargains.
missing_cases.why_the_instance_cannot_express_it: Residents have no other bargains in which a refusal here can cost them, so refusing is free and the resident's no-deal payoff is 0 by construction. The instance's reputation is implicit and one-sided (repetition with the same fleet); it has no channel by which a resident's conduct is observed and priced elsewhere.
missing_cases.smallest_change_that_would: A refusal penalty r_i paid outside the bargain by any resident who does not consent, r = (1, 1, 1), under a fleet take-it-or-leave-it at k = 3, baseline otherwise.
missing_cases.why_it_matters_for_the_question: The fleet offers h_i - r_i + epsilon, which each resident accepts since -r_i + epsilon beats -r_i: transfers (0, 1.5, 3) = 4.5, fleet 9 on a pie of 6, every resident at -1 against the clean river, Nash product over the engineered origin epsilon-cubed times 9, which is 0, floor -1 against the true baseline [sure, computed]. This is a wealth-effect-like degradation of the outside option that the open system manufactures, and it is asymmetric: a fleet is scored by many residents who each meet it once, a resident is scored by a few platforms that see every bargain. More compute in the scoring layer, which the agenda would count as capability, lowers the floor.

missing_cases.case: E. Agents with their own payoffs: one vendor serves the three residents (or both sides), and is paid by closed deals or by fees weighted toward richer clients.
missing_cases.why_the_instance_cannot_express_it: Each party's agent is identified with the party: four payoffs, four parties. There is no agent payoff distinct from a principal's, so common agency (one agent, several principals) and the vendor's cross-client trade-offs are inexpressible; Petel's 'one human, one principal, one agent' is assumed rather than tested.
missing_cases.smallest_change_that_would: A fifth payoff: the residents' shared agent earns a fee phi per closed deal (phi = 0.2) or a fee proportional to client wealth w0 = (10, 10, 2), and chooses the residents' joint demand. Baseline otherwise.
missing_cases.why_it_matters_for_the_question: A per-deal vendor accepts any offer that leaves its clients at or above no deal, so the fleet's take-it-or-leave-it lands at (6; 0, 0, 0), product 0, floor 0, the k = 3 veto gone without any change to k [sure, immediate]. A wealth-weighted vendor concedes resident 3's claim first. One vendor serving fleet and residents can trade one principal's outcome for another's (Bernheim and Whinston 1986 [likely, not read]). Whose compute it is, and who pays for it, decides whom its capability serves; 'give everyone an agent' says nothing about the agent's own incentives.

missing_cases.case: F. Endogenous budget ratio: the estimation dial is set by how many bargains each side has been in. The fleet's estimate of the s_i profile improves with every neighbourhood it has served; each resident's estimate of p_t is formed once, and a resident's attention is split across all the bargains they are in at the same time.
missing_cases.why_the_instance_cannot_express_it: The finite-budget switch takes c_f : c_N from an exogenous set {1:1, 10:1, 1:10}, so symmetry is one arm among three and chosen by the experimenter. The open system fixes the ratio: a party in M bargains of the same type has M times the samples, and a party in M bargains of different types has one M-th the budget per bargain.
missing_cases.smallest_change_that_would: Tie the budgets to bargain counts: c_f = M times c_N for the fleet's M neighbourhoods, and c_N divided by the number B of simultaneous bargains a resident is in; report the instance's errors at M = 10, B = 3 (fleet error 0.32 against resident error 1.7 when sigma = 1 and c_N = 1).
missing_cases.why_it_matters_for_the_question: The state's one condition under which the null survives is symmetric dials. In the open system the estimation dial is asymmetric by arithmetic, not by assumption, and the asymmetry grows with the number of bargains, which is exactly what the agenda scales. Which party gains follows the state's own reading: the bigger sampler. The case should be entered as the mechanism behind the 10:1 arm rather than as a new number.

missing_cases.case: G. Parties not at the table: rerouting exports harm. The reroute cost of 3 per slot is partly a cost to the fleet (c) and partly harm to a neighbourhood B that has no seat in the bargain (3 - c).
missing_cases.why_the_instance_cannot_express_it: The outside option switch books the whole 3 as the fleet's own cost, so a deal that reroutes is efficient for the four at the table and for the world alike. The instance has no fourth party who bears a cost without consenting, and so cannot express a Coasean deal that is better for its parties and worse in total.
missing_cases.smallest_change_that_would: Split the reroute cost: fleet pays c, neighbourhood B (not a party) suffers 3 - c per rerouted slot; run c in {3, 1.5, 1} under the outside option switch, baseline otherwise.
missing_cases.why_it_matters_for_the_question: At c = 3 the table reroutes only the night slot and total surplus is 8, the true optimum. At c = 1.5 the four at the table reroute every slot: apparent surplus 12.5, true surplus 6.5, harm of 6 exported to B; at c = 1 apparent 14.5, true 6.5, harm 8 on B [sure, computed by slot]. The Nash product among the parties rises with every unit of harm exported, and more compute spent finding reroutes raises it further. 'Better, and for whom' needs a line for those outside the bargain, which is the regulatory interest the agenda proposes to retire; without it the criterion rewards externalising. (Jehiel and Moldovanu on bargaining with externalities on outsiders is the candidate primary [unsure, not read].)

missing_cases.case: H. The author of the form as a player: the platform that fixes the clause menu, the consent rule and the standard terms is itself in every bargain and has a payoff, and a form once adopted persists across different counterparties.
missing_cases.why_the_instance_cannot_express_it: The no-enforcer switch has a platform that enforces and fixes clause language, but the platform is a mechanism with no payoff and the menu is chosen by the experimenter; k is likewise exogenous. The recurring switch carries a convention across periods with the same parties, not across bargains with different parties, so 'already set the convention' has no representation.
missing_cases.smallest_change_that_would: Give the platform a payoff (a fee per closed deal, or a share of transfers) and let it choose among the three clause menus (four slots, day/night, all-or-nothing, worth 6, 5.5 and 5.5 at best) and between k = 2 and k = 3, before the parties bargain; carry its choice to the next neighbourhood unchanged.
missing_cases.why_it_matters_for_the_question: The clause menu is worth 0.5 of a pie of 6 and the consent rule decides whether a resident's floor is 0 or -h_i; whoever sets them captures the constitutional choice the essay's river section defers. A platform paid per closed deal prefers the menu and rule that close most deals, not the ones that maximise the product; a platform that is also the fleet's vendor (case E) prefers the fleet's. This is the row that connects Krier's standard forms to the incumbent reading: the form is a commitment device for whoever writes it.

missing_cases.case: I. Exit for the weak side, priced by wealth: a resident can move away at a cost m_i, and resident 3 cannot afford to.
missing_cases.why_the_instance_cannot_express_it: The fleet has an outside option (reroute at 3 per slot) and the residents have none; under the switch as written the fleet's unilateral reroute of all four slots is worth 6.5 against a joint optimum of 8, so the pie over no deal is already 1.5 and the equal gain 0.375 (product 0.02), with the residents' floor still 0 by the rule. An asymmetry of outside options is a dial the mission's four do not name and the instance cannot vary on the residents' side.
missing_cases.smallest_change_that_would: A move cost m_i per resident, m = (3, 3, 3), payable only from the endowment w0 = (10, 10, 2) when wealth effects are on, so resident 3 cannot move.

Switches: all off (parametric, once, linear money, enforcer assumed, closed) in every number below unless stated; the instance's baseline is confirmed by enumeration of the sixteen schedules (pie 6 at MDE, 5.5 at MDEN; arbitrary switch: pie 5 at MD, MDE falls to 4.5). Krier's best reply, against my finding: his secondary institutions are exactly the missing conditions, supplied explicitly. On the instance it holds row by row: a bargaining club spanning neighbourhoods answers case B by making the two triples one bloc; a standard form answers case A by fixing terms the fleet cannot vary from neighbourhood to neighbourhood; courts answer D and G by forbidding refusal-scoring and giving neighbourhood B standing; an option fee paid to every candidate neighbourhood before the fleet chooses restores part of the residents' share in B. What the reply concedes is the essay: none of these arises from giving everyone an agent; each is authored before the bargain by someone, and the natural author of a standard form or a club's constitution is the party in many bargains (cases A, H), so the institution reproduces the asymmetry unless a third party writes it; courts with standing for non-parties are the regulation the agenda proposed to retire; and the origin against which 'better' is measured is itself set by these institutions (cases C, D), so the agenda cannot claim its outcome is better by default, only better given institutions it does not supply.

Answer to the mission question, on the instance: more computation produces better outcomes, a higher Nash product of gains over no deal and a higher floor, when the system is closed and the dials symmetric: one bargain, parties whose only stakes are at the table, a no-deal origin fixed by the rule, and nobody carrying history, forms or reputation in from elsewhere. The open system removes each of those by construction rather than by assumption. The party in many bargains is the long-run player (A: (6; 0, 0, 0), product 0), the bigger sampler (F: the 10:1 budget arm is M = 10 neighbourhoods), the shopper between counterparties (B: residents' share 0 with unanimity intact), the author of the form (H), and the one who can move the no-deal origin by bundling (C: resident 3 at -0.25 where the unbundled split gave +1.5, while the product rises from 5.06 to 57) or by scoring refusals (D: every resident at -1 against the clean river); parties outside the bargain bear what the deal exports (G: harm of 6 to 8 on a neighbourhood with no seat, while the product at the table rises); and the weak side's outside option is bought with wealth it may not have (I). So in the open system compute favours whoever is in the most bargains, on the instance the fleet, and among residents it costs most to resident 3, the most harmed and poorest, in every case where the origin moves. The criterion's origin, gains over no deal, is itself a strategic variable there, which the mission should record as a third blind spot of the product beside the two already noted. Each of the nine changes above is one line on the instance; A and B are computable by hand, and A is the chain-store sequel the state already names.
